p0.original: 关键问题：人们会使用哪些理论来理解自己和他人
p0.en: Key issues: What theories people use to understand themselves and others

p2.original: 我们对自己和他人的了解是以内隐人格理论和自我叙述为基础的，这两者都受到社会文化的影响。
p2.en: Our understanding of ourselves and others is based on the theory of implicit personality and self-presentation, both of which are influenced by socio-cultural factors.

p3.original: 我们已经知道心理学家是如何看待人格的了。但是，普通人是如何理解他人和自己的呢？不论对错，我们经常会做出一些关于他人或自己人格的假设。例如，当你约会、应聘工作，或者第一次见到你的老师或同学时，你总会这么做。我们还想知道的是，其他社会文化中的成员对人格的看法是否与我们类似。这些问题很重要，因为用来理解人格的“民间理论”或内隐人格理论（implicit personality theory）可以维持或损害人与人，甚至是国家与国家之间的关系。我们的核心概念是：
p3.en: We already know what psychologists think about people. But how do ordinary people understand others and themselves? Whether we are right or wrong, we often make assumptions about others or our own personalities. For example, you always do this when you're dating, applying for a job, or seeing your teacher or classmate for the first time. We would also like to know whether other members of the socio-cultural community have a similar view of personality. These issues are important, because the “civil theory” or the implicit theory of personality, which is used to understand the personality, can maintain or damage the relationship between the person and the person, even between the State and the State. Our core concepts are:

p4.original: 我们对自己和他人的了解是以内隐人格理论和自我叙述为基础的，这两者都受到社会文化的影响。
p4.en: Our understanding of ourselves and others is based on the theory of implicit personality and self-presentation, both of which are influenced by socio-cultural factors.

p5.original: 接下来，首先让我们了解一下用来理解他人的内隐人格理论。
p5.en: Let's start with the theory of hidden personality that is used to understand others.

p7.original: 10.13 了解内隐人格理论的重要性。
p7.en: 10.13 Understanding the importance of the theory of implicit personality.

p8.original: 10.14 了解为什么自我叙述是人格的一部分。
p8.en: 10.14 Understanding why self-presentation is part of the personality.

p9.original: 10.15 评估个体主义和集体主义文化对人格的影响。
p9.en: 10.15 Assess the impact of individualism and collectiveism on the personality.

p12.original: 了解内隐人格理论的重要性。
p12.en: Understanding the importance of the theory of implicit personality.

p13.original: 想想你曾经的榜样，再想想那些让你无法忍受的人。在这两种情况下，你是否会将某些人格特质与他们联系起来：诚实、可靠、幽默、慷慨、外向、攻击性、情绪化、悲观等。甚至在幼儿时期，你就有了一个初级的人格评价系统。因此，你能够确定新认识的人将会是朋友还是敌人；通过解读父母或老师的人格特征，你会习得与他们和谐相处的方式。
p13.en: Think of your role models, and think of those who make you unbearable. In both cases, do you link certain personality characteristics to them: honesty, reliability, humor, generosity, outward orientation, aggressiveness, emotionalization, pessimism, etc. Even in early childhood, you have a primary personality assessment system. So you can determine whether the new person you know will be a friend or an enemy; By interpreting the identity of parents or teachers, you learn to live in harmony with them.

p14.original: 在这些情况下，你正是在使用内隐人格理论对他人的人格做出判断。具体而言，在评价他人的人格时，你会将他人的行为与你所认为的他们拥有的特质联系起来。像内隐记忆一样，我们在使用内隐人格理论时，很大程度上是无意识的，所以对他人的人格进行判断并不是一件困难的事（Fiske & Neuberg，1990；Macrae et al.，1994）。
p14.en: In these cases, it is in the use of the implicit personality theory that you judge the personality of others. In particular, when assessing the personality of others, you relate the behaviour of others to what you believe they have. As with our inner memory, we are largely unconscious in our use of the hidden personality theory, so it is not difficult to judge the personality of others (Fiske & Neuberg, 1990); Macrae et al., 1994.

p15.original: 在很多时候，我们使用内隐人格理论足够让自己的社会关系保持稳定（至少在熟悉的环境中如此）。虽然在不熟悉的环境中，我们的预测可能不是那么准确。但在熟悉的环境中，内隐人格理论能够帮助我们预测他人的动机和行为、完成工作、购买早餐、完成学业，以及与朋友交流。在某些方面，内隐人格理论可能和大五人格理论没什么区别。在一项研究中，大学生需要对一些他们只见过但不认识的同学进行人格评价，他们的评价结果与通过大五人格量表得出的结果非常一致（Mehl et al.，2006）。这里有一个有趣的例外：过分自信或争辩行为被视为男性情绪稳定的标志，但对女性而言却会被认为是情绪不稳定的标志。
p15.en: In many cases, we use the theory of implicit personality enough to stabilize our social relations (at least in the familiar environment). Although in an unfamiliar environment, our projections may not be as accurate. But in a familiar environment, the theory of hidden personality can help us to predict the motives and behaviour of others, to complete our work, to buy breakfast, to complete our studies and to communicate with friends. In some respects, the theory of implicit personality may be no different from the theory of the first five. In a study, university students were required to perform personality evaluations of students they had only met but not known, and their findings were very consistent with those obtained through the five-person scale (Mehl et al., 2006). There is an interesting exception: over-confidence or controversial behaviour is seen as a sign of emotional stability for men, but for women it can be seen as a sign of emotional instability.

p16.original: 内隐人格理论也有其他缺点。依据朴素的假设以及有关特质和外貌方面的刻板印象对人格进行推测时，我们有可能会出错（Hochwalder，1995）。因此，我们可能会错误地认为身高体壮的人很快乐，或者金发碧眼的人智商不高。我们也可能会错误地认为某些特质总是一起出现，如有创造力与情绪不稳定。
p16.en: There are other shortcomings in the theory of implicit personality. We may be at risk of error when speculating on our personality on the basis of simple assumptions and stereotypes about the quality and appearance (Hochwalder, 1995). Therefore, we may mistakenly think that tall people are happy, or that blonde people are less intelligent. We may also wrongly believe that certain qualities always appear together, with creativity and emotional instability.

p17.original: 我们用内隐理论对他人进行人格判断时，若投射了个人的动机和情感，会得出错误的结论。因此，一个感到愤怒、快乐或沮丧的人可能会认为其他人也持有同样的感觉。
p17.en: When we judge others by their own inner theory, the wrong conclusion is reached when the individual's motives and emotions are projected. Thus, one person who feels anger, joy or frustration may think that others share the same feeling.

p18.original: 最后，在人格特质是固定的还是可变的这一问题上，内隐人格理论也可能会造成矛盾。相较于那些认为特质可以改变的人，那些相信特质稳定不变的人更有可能产生“刻板印象”（Levy et al.，1998；Molden & Dweck，2006）。人格到底是固定的还是可变的呢？不同的假设会对父母养育孩子、老师教导学生，以及领导管理员工产生不同的影响。
p18.en: Finally, the theory of implicit personality may also create contradictions on the question of whether personality characteristics are fixed or variable. Those who believe that the quality remains stable are more likely to produce “stereotyping” than those who believe that the quality can change” (Levy et al., 1998); Mulden & Dweck, 2006. Is the personality fixed or variable? Different assumptions have different effects on parents raising children, teachers teaching students, and leadership and management staff.

p20.original: 卡罗尔·德韦克（Carol Dweck，2006，2007）经过长达20年的研究发现，我们的思维模式（mindset）并不是人格中无足轻重的部分，而是我们整个心理世界的一个重要方面。它能帮助我们设立目标，影响我们对未来的看法（积极的还是消极的），甚至还决定我们是否能发挥自己的潜力。当你和你的父母、老师或教练认为某项天赋或能力是“固定的”时，会发生什么呢？如果你和他们都相信你是一个智商很高的人，你从小就是一个音乐天才、一个超级田径明星或者一个有天赋的作家。你天生就有某种能力，不需要努力就能成功，那么你可能就不会那么努力、不再练习，当竞争不那么激烈的时候，你可能在一开始做得很好。另一种是“成长型”思维模式的孩子：他和他身边的其他人都认为，任何天赋或能力都是不断发展的，都可以通过不断的练习和努力得到提升。假设“固定型”和“成长型”思维模式的人都遭遇了失败。成长型思维的孩子可能会认为，想要取得进步，就必须更加努力地学习，花更多的时间练习。而“固定型”思维的孩子则会认为，失败是由于自己能力不够，这会让那些判定他天生优秀的人失望。正如德韦克教授在TED演讲中所说的那样：“成长型思维就是相信自己可以进步。”
p20.en: After 20 years of research, Carol Dweck, 2006 and 2007, it was found that our mindset (mindset) was not a insignificant part of the human personality, but an important aspect of our entire psychological world. It can help us set goals, influence our vision of the future (positive or negative) and even determine whether we can realize our potential. What happens when you and your parents, teachers or coach think that a gift or ability is “fixed”? If you and they both believe you're a highly intelligent person, you've been a musical genius, a super track star or a talented writer since childhood. You're born with some kind of ability, and you don't need to work hard to succeed, so you probably won't try so hard, you won't practice so much, and you might do well at the beginning when the competition is less intense. Another child is the “growth” mode of thinking: he and everyone else around him believe that any gift or ability is evolving and can be enhanced through continuous exercise and effort. People who assume that “fixed” and “growth” thinking patterns have failed. Growing-minded children may think that to make progress it is necessary to learn more and spend more time practicing. For their part, children with “fixed” thinking would argue that failure is due to their lack of capacity, which would disappoint those who judge that he is born to be good. As Professor Dewey said in his TED speech, “The growth thinking is the belief that you can make progress.

p21.original: 畅销书作家马尔科姆·格拉德威尔（Malcolm Gladwell）在他的《异类》（Outliers，2008）中阐述了这样的观点：那些被视为天才并取得了成功的年轻人与那些未能实现预期潜力的年轻人之间的主要区别在于有没有进行过10000小时的练习。但是，新的心理干预可以在短时间内改变思维模式，从而提高成绩并减少从数学到运动等多个领域的成就差异（Dweck，2008）。
p21.en: Malcolm Gladwell, the best-selling writer, has stated in his "Outliers, 2008 " that the main difference between young people who are considered talented and successful and those who fail to realize their expected potential is whether 10,000 hours of practice have been practiced. However, new psychological interventions can change mindsets in a short period of time, thereby increasing achievement and reducing disparities in achievement in many areas, from mathematics to sports (Dweck, 2008).

p22.original: 10.14 自我叙述：我们自己的人格故事

p24.original: 了解为什么自我叙述是人格的一部分。
p24.en: To understand why self-presentation is part of the personality.

p25.original: 当有人说“介绍一下你自己”时，你会怎样回应呢？你可能会介绍自己是哪里人，业余时间喜欢做什么，以及你的职业目标是什么。但如果你问自己这个问题，你会如何回答呢？心理学家丹·麦克亚当斯（Dan McAdams）将自己讲述关于自己的故事称之为“自我叙述”（self-narrative）。他认为自我叙述是人格的一个成分，就像动机、情绪或社会关系一样重要。自我叙述实际上是一个比自我更广泛的概念，是一个关于自我概念随时间而变化的故事。自我叙述把人格的各个要素联系在一起，就像将珍珠串成项链那样。麦克亚当斯还说，贯穿我们一生的自我叙述是我们自我认同的基础，由此给予了我们同一性和目标感。
p25.en: How do you respond when someone says, "Bring yourself in"? You might describe where you are, what you like to do in your leisure time, and what your professional goals are. But if you ask yourself that, how will you answer that? Dan McAdams, a psychologist, described his story as “self-narrative”. He considers self-statement to be an integral part of the personality, as important as motivation, emotion or social relations. Self-narrative is in fact a broader concept than self-image, a story of self-image changing over time. Self-narratives link the elements of the personality, as they tie pearls into necklaces. MacAdams added that self-narratives throughout our lives are the basis of our self-identification, giving us a sense of unity and purpose.

p26.original: 当然，当我们为自己讲述自我叙述的故事时，文化会产生很大的影响。虽然麦克亚当斯还没有做过更广泛的跨文化研究，但他已经确定在美国文化中有一个特别重要的自我叙述，那就是救赎的自我（redemptive self）。
p26.en: Of course, when we tell ourselves our own stories, culture has a great impact. Although MacAdams has not done a broader cross-cultural study, he has determined that there is a particularly important self-statement in American culture, that is, the self-recoverable self.

p27.original: 并不是每个人的自我叙述都遵循救赎的自我模式。但麦克亚当斯在生育期成年人身上总会发现这种模式。生育期成年人最初被发展心理学家爱利克·埃里克森（Erik Erikson）用来形容有繁衍能力的健康成年人。更具体地说，繁衍力形容的是那些关心自身之外的社会和下一代福利的成年人。在其他的文化中，健康成年人的自我叙述特点还有待研究。
p27.en: Not everyone's self-narrative follows the self-style of salvation. But MacAdams always finds this pattern in adults who have given birth. Adults of childbearing age were initially used by development psychologist Erik Erikson to describe healthy adults with productive capacity. More specifically, reproduction describes adults who care for the well-being of society and the next generation beyond themselves. In other cultures, self-narrative characteristics of healthy adults have yet to be studied.

p28.en: 10.15 The impact of culture on the perception of personality

p30.original: 评估个体主义和集体主义文化对人格的影响。
p30.en: Assessing the impact of individualism and collectiveism on the personality.

p31.original: 众所周知，西方人倾向于把个人或自我作为人格的核心。虽然世界各地的人们都认同自我的独特性。但是很多人，尤其是那些生活在集体主义文化中的人，认为自我通常是融入更大的社会网络中的。他们认为，如果一个人与他人存在社会联结，那么就不能跨过他人单独了解他。在这里我们不得不提到跨文化心理学家亨利·特里安德斯（Harry Triandis）。
p31.en: It is well known that Westerners tend to place individuals or themselves at the centre of their personality. Although people around the world recognize their own uniqueness. But many people, especially those living in a collective culture, think that they are usually integrated into the larger social network. In their view, if a person has social ties with others, then he cannot be understood alone across others. Here we have to mention the cross-cultural psychologist, Harry Triandis.

p32.original: 10.15.1 个体主义、集体主义和人格

p33.original: 在特里安德斯（Triandis，1995）看来，文化差异最根本的维度是个体主义和集体主义。对于那些在欧美传统文化中长大的人来说，个人是社会的基本单位，而亚洲、南美和非洲文化则更重视家庭或其他团体。在集体主义文化中，人们更倾向于保持和促进团体和谐，并希望其他人也是如此。在个体主义文化中，人们认为自己有一个独立于社会关系的独特身份（Pedersen，1979）。因此，对于欧美国家的人来说，自我就是一个整体，对于亚洲和非洲的许多地区的人来说，自我只是集体的一部分（Cohen & Gunz，2002）。
p33.en: From the perspective of Triandis, 1995, the most fundamental dimensions of cultural differences are individualism and collectivism. For those who have grown up in traditional cultures in Europe and the United States, the individual is the basic unit of society, while Asian, South American and African cultures place greater emphasis on the family or other groups. In a collectiveist culture, there is a greater tendency to maintain and promote group harmony, and it is hoped that others will do the same. In an individualistic culture, one considers itself to have a unique identity independent of social relations (Pedersen, 1979). Thus, for people in Europe and the United States, self is a whole and for people in many parts of Asia and Africa, self is only a part of the collective (Cohen & Gunz, 2002).

p34.original: 然而，新的跨文化研究表明，亚洲各地并不都是统一的集体主义文化。在学者托马斯·托尔赫姆（Thomas Talhelm）看来，最好的解释是“大米理论”。托尔赫姆认为，有着数百年历史的中国南方的复杂灌溉系统和种植水稻需要共享灌溉水资源这件事促进了社会协作，而北方种植小麦只需要依靠自然降雨，因此中国南方需要的合作水平比北方更高（Doucleff，2014；Talhelm et al.，2014）。不过，大米理论的基础是相关关系，这意味着我们并不能确切地说观察到的文化差异就一定是历史上的耕作模式导致的。此外，我们也必须清楚，这只是一项研究，我们还需要做更多的研究来验证大米理论是否合理。
p34.en: However, new cross-cultural studies have shown that there is not always a unified collectiveist culture throughout Asia. According to Thomas Talhelm, the best explanation is the “rice theory”. Tolheim believes that the complex irrigation systems and the need to share irrigation water resources for rice cultivation in the south of China, which has a centuries-old history, have promoted social collaboration, while the cultivation of wheat in the north has to rely on natural rainfall, and therefore the level of cooperation in the south of China needs to be higher than in the north (Doucleff, 2014); Talhelm et al., 2014). However, the rice theory is based on relationships, which means that the cultural differences that we do not accurately observe must have been the result of historical farming patterns. Furthermore, we must be clear that this is only a study and that we need to do more to validate the logic of the rice theory.

p35.original: 我们应该清楚：并不是说集体主义或个体主义哪一个更好。从不同的角度来看，每一种文化都各有优劣。集体主义文化鼓励共同努力，通常注重工作或家庭等群体的利益和荣誉。此外，像玛丽·卡尔金斯这样挑战社会规范的人，更有可能在个体主义文化中取得成功。
p35.en: We should be clear: it is not what is better than collectivism or individualism. From different perspectives, each culture has its own advantages and disadvantages. A collectiveist culture encourages joint efforts, usually focusing on the interests and honours of groups such as work or the family. Moreover, those who challenge social norms, such as Mary Carlkins, are more likely to succeed in an individualistic culture.

p36.original: 文化如何影响人格 人们的人格和行为在很多方面的表现都来源于他们是处于集体主义还是个体主义文化中。所以，在对他人进行评价的时候，美国人和欧洲人往往会犯基本归因错误（Fundamental Attribution Error，FAE）。这种基本归因错误反映在两个方面：它高估了行为的人格（内部）原因，同时低估了社会环境（外部）因素。这种误解源于一种假设，即他人的行为，尤其是令人讨厌的、笨拙的、不恰当的或其他不受欢迎的行为，是由他们的人格而不是所处的环境造成的。如果你在美国上心理学课迟到了，其他学生可能会认为你是一个拖延或没有规划的人。但如果你在日本上心理学课迟到了，其他学生更有可能认为是一些外部原因导致了你的行为，如交通问题。总体来说，基本归因错误在拉丁美洲或亚洲等集体主义文化中不太普遍（Church et al.，2005；Lillard，1997）。
p36.en: How culture affects the personhood of people in many ways is the expression of their personality and behaviour in the culture of collectivism or individualism. Thus, Americans and Europeans tend to make fundamental attribution mistakes when evaluating others (Fundamental Actor, FAE). This basic attribution error is reflected in two ways: it overestimates the personality (internal) of the act and underestimates the social environment (external). This misunderstanding stems from the assumption that the behaviour of others, particularly the abhorrent, clumsy, inappropriate or other undesirable behaviour, is caused by their personality rather than by the circumstances in which they live. If you're late for psychology classes in the United States, other students may think you're a delayed or unplanned person. But if you're late for psychology classes in Japan, other students are more likely to believe that external causes such as traffic problems have led to your behavior. In general, errors of attribution are less common in collective cultures such as Latin America or Asia (Church et al., 2005); Lillard, 1997.

p37.original: 文化的差异还体现在其他维度。例如，如果要在竞争和合作之间做出选择，崇尚个体主义的美国人通常会选择竞争（Aronson，2004；Gallo & McClintock，1965）。一般而言，美国人的成就需求也高于集体主义文化中的人。
p37.en: Cultural differences are also reflected in other dimensions. For example, if there is to be a choice between competition and cooperation, individualist Americans usually choose competition (Aronson, 2004); Gallo & McClintock, 1965. In general, American demands for achievement are also higher than those in a collective culture.

p38.original: 不同的文化对“理想人格”也有不同的看法（Matsumoto，1996）。在西方心理学传统中，心理健康是人格中对立部分和冲突部分的整合。这一点在弗洛伊德主义和荣格主义的理论中表现得尤为明显。相比之下，一些亚洲心理学家，尤其是那些与佛教有关的心理学家，则寻求相反的结果：将意识从感觉和对世俗经验的记忆中分离出来（Gardiner et al.，1998；Pedersen，1979）。
p38.en: Different cultures also have different views on “ideal personality” (Matsumo, 1996). In Western psychology traditions, mental health is a combination of the opposite and conflict parts of the personality. This is particularly evident in Freudist and vanity theories. By contrast, some Asian psychologists, especially those associated with Buddhism, seek the opposite: to separate consciousness from feelings and memories of secular experience (Gardiner et al., 1998); Pedersen, 1979.

p39.original: 以下是世界各地的人在人格上的差异。
p39.en: The following are the differences in human personality around the world.

p40.original: 不同年龄段和性别人群的地位。在许多亚洲和美洲原住民文化中，老年人的地位更高。许多非西方社会中的女性处于次等地位（Segall et al.，1999）。
p40.en: Status of the population by age group and sex. In many Asian and Native American cultures, older persons have a higher status. Women in many non-Western societies are in a lower position (Segall et al., 1999).

p41.original: 爱情。虽然所有文化中都有爱情，但是直到近代欧洲才强调爱情是婚姻的基础。这也最常出现在个体主义文化中（Hatfeld & Rapson，1998；Rosenblatt，1966）。
p41.en: Love. Although love existed in all cultures, it had not been emphasized in recent Europe that it was the basis of marriage. This is also most frequently found in individualistic cultures (Hatfeld & Rapson, 1998); Rosenblatt, 1966.

p42.original: 情绪的表达。在亚洲文化中，强烈的情感倾向于被压抑（Tsai & Uemura，1988）；而欧美人尽管存在明显的性别差异，但总体上仍然更倾向于将强烈情绪表达出来。
p42.en: Emotional expression. In Asian culture, strong emotions tend to be suppressed (Tsai & Uemura, 1988); In general, Europeans tend to express strong emotions, despite the obvious gender differences.

p43.original: 控制源。与墨西哥等发展中国家的个体相比，美国、加拿大等工业化国家的个体更倾向于有内部控制源（Berry et al.，1992；Draguns，1979；Shiraev & Levy，2004）。
p43.en: Control the source. Individuals in industrialized countries such as the United States and Canada tend to have a source of internal control over individuals in developing countries such as Mexico (Berry et al., 1992); Draguins, 1979; Shiraev & Levy, 2004.

p44.original: 思维和情感。许多文化（如拉丁美洲文化）中的人并不像美国人那样对想法和情绪有强烈且明显的区别（Fajans，1985；Lutz，1988）。
p44.en: Thinking and emotion. People in many cultures (e.g. Latin American) do not have the same strong and obvious difference between thought and emotion as Americans (Fajans, 1985); Lutz, 1988.

p45.original: 社会和谐。亚洲文化强调社会互动中的和谐，但在西方文化中这是一种从众行为。西方文化重视社会比较中的独特性，而在亚洲文化中这似乎是一种异常行为（Kim & Markus，1999）。
p45.en: Social harmony. Asian culture emphasizes harmony in social interaction, but in Western culture it is an act of public opinion. Western cultures value the uniqueness of social comparisons, which appear to be an anomaly in Asian cultures (Kim & Markus, 1999).

p46.original: 尽管存在这些差异，我们是否可以说世界各地的人从根本上讲是一样的吗？你有什么看法？
p46.en: Despite these differences, can we say that people around the world are fundamentally the same? What do you think?

p47.original: 在神经元和大脑回路的层面，答案当然是肯定的。但人格也被文化影响，所以更全面的答案是：“不完全是这样，但也许可以在一些相同的维度上对他们进行描述。”文化指的是所有成员共享、熟悉并传递给下一代的社会内容。人格是特质的独特整合，这些特质能够在一些文化中将个体区分开来（Brislin，1981，pp.51-52）。
p47.en: At the neurons and brain circuits, of course, the answer is yes. But the personality is also influenced by culture, so the more comprehensive answer is: “Not entirely, but perhaps they can be described at some of the same dimensions. “Culture refers to the social content that all members share, become familiar with and transmit to the next generation. Personality is a unique combination of attributes that allow individuals to be distinguished in a number of cultures (Brislin, 1981, pp. 51-52).

p48.original: 但不要忘记，文化和人格是相互作用的。文化塑造着身在其中的个体的人格，正如个体可以影响文化一样。所以，在某种程度上，人格是个体所在社会的价值观、态度、信仰、道德习俗、工作、养育方式、攻击性、成就、竞争、死亡，以及其他许多对人类都很重要的东西的综合产物。因此，从广义上说，文化就是一个社会的“人格”（Benedict，1934）。
p48.en: But remember that culture and personality interact. Culture shapes the personality of the individual within it, just as it can influence it. To some extent, therefore, the personality is the product of the values, attitudes, beliefs, moral practices, work, upbringing, aggressiveness, achievement, competition, death and many other things that matter to humanity. Thus, in a broad sense, culture is the “personal personality” of a society (Benedict, 1934).

p49.original: 心理学很有用 当人格出现障碍时
p49.en: Psychology works when a personality disorder occurs.

p50.original: 人格障碍可以解释很多历史或公众人物的异常行为，包括有多段婚姻的国王亨利八世、好莱坞的很多叛逆男孩和女孩，以及凶残杀手莉琪·波登（Lizzie Borden，她用一把斧头杀死了她的父母）。长期的判断失误、思维混乱、情绪不稳、社会关系受损或无法控制冲动等都是人格障碍（personality disorders）的症状（Clark，2009）。它的关键表现是长期适应不良的人格模式。在这里，我们列举了三种比较常见的人格障碍。
p50.en: The personality disorder can explain the unusual behaviour of many historical or public figures, including King Henry VIII, who has many marriages, many rebel boys and girls in Hollywood, and the murderous killer Lizzie Borden, who killed her parents with an axe. Long-term miscalculation, confusion, emotional instability, impairment of social relations or inability to control impulses are symptoms of personality impairments (Clark, 2009). Its key expression is the long-term adaptation of poor personality patterns. Here, we list three more common personality barriers.

p55.original: 在希腊神话中，纳西索斯（Narcissus）是一个非常迷恋自己俊美容貌的人，他经常在池塘边的倒影中自我欣赏，却在某次自我欣赏时不幸掉进水中淹死了。“自恋”这一术语由此而来，自恋表现为夸大自我的重要性，需要得到持续的关注或赞美，以及常常幻想成功或权力。患有自恋型人格障碍（narcissistic personality disorder）的人可能会对批评或小挫折做出不恰当的反应。他们通常不善于处理人际关系，觉得自己可以不履行义务，自私地利用别人，难以理解别人的感受。他们很少会自愿地进行临床治疗。从娱乐小报（很多方面并不可靠）上来看，电影和唱片行业中的许多从业者都患有自恋型人格障碍。
p55.en: Narcissus, a Greek myth, is a very fond man of his beauty, who often enjoys himself in a reflection by the pond, but unfortunately drowns in the water at one time. The term “narcissism” thus manifests itself as exaggerating the importance of self, requiring sustained attention or praise, and often fantasizing about success or power. People with narcissistic personality disorder may react inappropriately to criticism or minor frustrations. They are often not very good at dealing with relationships, and they feel that they can fail to fulfil their obligations and use others selfishly, making it difficult to understand their feelings. They rarely volunteer for clinical treatment. In the entertainment tabloids, which are not reliable in many respects, many of the practitioners in the film and record industry suffer from narcissistic personality disorders.

p57.original: 从冷酷的高管到骗子再到连环杀手，他们都可能患有反社会型人格障碍（antisocial personality disorder）。美国大概有3%的成年人患有反社会型人格障碍，但是他们当中的70%～80%已经进了监狱（Patrick，2007）。从犯罪行为的性别差异来说，男性被诊断为反社会型人格障碍的可能性是女性的四倍（Regier et al.，1988，1993）。
p57.en: From cold-blooded executives to liars to serial killers, they can all suffer from antisocial personality disorder. Around 3 per cent of adults in the United States suffer from anti-social personality disorders, but 70 to 80 per cent of them are in prison (Patrick, 2007). Men are four times more likely than women to be diagnosed with anti-social personality disorder in terms of gender differences in criminal behaviour (Regier et al., 1988, 1993).

p58.original: 患有反社会型人格障碍的人似乎缺乏良知或对他人的责任感。反社会型人格障碍者典型的表现是，他们早年就开始违反社会规范，如扰乱班级秩序、打架、离家出走。这些行为可能发展成更残忍的行为和对他人的肆意漠视，如故意破坏公共财产、虐待动物或放火。反社会型人格障碍的其他特征还表现为长期说谎和偷窃。
p58.en: Persons suffering from anti-social personality disorders appear to lack conscience or a sense of responsibility towards others. People with anti-social personality impairments are typically shown to have started to violate social norms early in life, such as disrupting class order, fighting and running away from home. These acts may develop into more brutal acts and indifference to others, such as deliberate destruction of public property, abuse of animals or arson. Other features of anti-social personality disorder are also manifested in long-term lies and theft.

p59.original: 即使有些患有反社会型人格障碍的个体可能已经发现自己常陷入麻烦，但他们可能也不会感到焦虑、羞愧或有任何强烈的负面情绪。事实上，在令正常人激动或心烦的情境中，他们却能保持冷静。那些表现出暴力或犯罪（如谋杀或其他重罪）的反社会型人格障碍者，通常被称为精神病态者或反社会者，尽管这种叫法没有被DSM-5认可（Krueger & Markon，2006；Miller，2008）。
p59.en: Even if some individuals with anti-social personality disorders may have found themselves in trouble, they may not be anxious, ashamed or have any strong negative feelings. In fact, they can remain calm in situations that exasperate or distraught normal people. Those who display anti-social personality disorder by violence or crime (such as murder or other felony) are generally referred to as either mentally ill or anti-social, although this is not recognized by DSM-5 (Krueger & Markon, 2006); Miller, 2008.

p60.original: 反社会型人格障碍虽然通常出现在罪犯身上，但在成功的政治家和商人中也很常见，这些人把事业、金钱和权力凌驾于所有人和事之上（Babiak & Hare，2006；Patrick，2007）。有些人很有魅力，他们会利用自己的魅力来获得别人的信任。也是由于这些特征，他们可以逃避时间较长的牢狱之灾，当他们被抓住时，通常会使用一些手段来摆脱麻烦。
p60.en: Anti-social personality disorder, although usually found in criminals, is common among successful politicians and businessmen who have given priority to cause, money and power over everyone (Babiak & Hare, 2006); Patrick, 2007. Some people are charming and they use their charm to gain the trust of others. These characteristics also allow them to escape from longer prison conditions, and when they are caught, they usually use some means to escape from trouble.

p61.original: 是什么导致了反社会型人格障碍？神经成像的研究表明，反社会者的杏仁核和眶额皮层出现了功能异常（Kiehl & Buckholtz，2010；Raine，2008）。然而，我们还不知道这是反社会型人格障碍的原因还是结果。
p61.en: What leads to anti-social personality disorder? Research on neuroimaging shows that antisocial almond cores and anatomy cortex have function abnormalities (Kiehl & Buckholtz, 2010); Raine, 2008. However, we do not yet know whether this is the cause or the result of anti-social personality disorders.

p63.original: 人格障碍的第三种类型是边缘型人格障碍（borderline personality disorder）。患边缘型人格障碍的人，在人际关系上是不稳定的、易冲动的和混乱的（Butcher et al.，2010；Selby & Joiner，2009）。边缘型人格障碍者的情绪变化无常，还有冲突不断的人际关系。当他人没能满足他们的需求时，他们会非常的失落，并会攻击和辱骂对方。他们对挫折也缺乏承受力。他们的冲动可能表现为滥用药物、赌博、性滥交、暴饮暴食、莽撞驾驶、自伤或企图自杀。脑成像研究甚至在边缘型人格障碍者大脑中发现了与此相关的变异（Bower，2009；Meyer-Lindenberg，2008）。
p63.en: The third type of personality disorder is the marginal personality disorder. People suffering from marginal personality disorders are unstable, impulsive and disordered in human relations (Butcher et al., 2010); Selby & Joaner, 2009. People with marginal personality impairments are subject to volatile moods and to ongoing conflict. When others fail to meet their needs, they are very disappointed and attack and insult each other. They also lack resilience to setbacks. Their impulses may be manifested in drug abuse, gambling, sexual abuse, drinking, reckless driving, self-inflicted injuries or attempted suicide. A related mutation was found in brain imaging studies and even in the brain of people with marginal personality impairments (Bower, 2009); Meyer-Lindenberg, 2008.

p64.original: 在你认识的人中可能就有边缘型人格障碍者。事实上，边缘型人格障碍者约占成年人总数的2%，占临床患者的10%～20%（Meyer-Lindenberg，2009；National Institute of Mental Health，2010b）。不幸的是，就像其他人格障碍一样，目前边缘型人格障碍的治疗前景并不乐观，并且边缘型人格障碍者极少寻求帮助或持续接受治疗。
p64.en: There may be marginal personality impairments among people you know. In fact, marginal personality impairments account for about 2 per cent of all adults and account for 10-20 per cent of clinical patients (Meyer-Lindenberg, 2009); National Institute of Central Health, 2010b. Unfortunately, as is the case with other people's handicaps, the current prospects for treatment of marginal personality impairments are not promising, and those with marginal personality impairments rarely seek help or continue to receive treatment.

p65.original: 批判性思维的应用：人格-情境争论
p65.en: Application of critical thinking: personality-situation debate

p66.original: 认知理论学家沃尔特·米歇尔提出的证据表明，我们的行为在不同情境下的一致性远远低于预期，这无异于向人格理论学家们丢了一枚科学炸弹（Mischel，1968，1973，2003）。一个在聚会上表现外向的人，在课堂上可能会变得害羞和腼腆。你的“神经质”的朋友可能会在你陷入危机时成为你的支柱。就像莎士比亚的《皆大欢喜》中的罗莎琳德（Rosalind）一样，一个人在不同的情况和不同的人面前，会展现出不同的人格。因此，米歇尔认为，在预测一个人的行为时，对情境的了解比对人的特质的了解更重要。后来，在人格心理学领域就出现了人格-情境争论（person-situation controrersy，Pervin，1985）。
p66.en: The evidence presented by cognitive theorist Walter Michel suggests that our behaviour is well below expectations in different contexts, amounting to the loss of a scientific bomb to personality theorists (Mischel, 1968, 1973, 2003). A person who behaves outwardly at a party may become shy and shy in the classroom. Your “nervous” friends could be your back when you're in crisis. Like Rosalind in Shakespeare's "Happy", a person presents a different personality in a different context and in a different person. Thus, Michelle believes that knowledge of the situation is more important than knowledge of the human nature when predicting the behaviour of a person. Later, there was a personality-situation dispute in the area of personality psychology (person-situation control, Pervin, 1985).

p67.original: 米歇尔的主张挑战了大多数人格理论的基础。毕竟，如果人们在不同的情境下表现出的行为不一致，那么人格理论又有什么用呢？难道人格没有持续性吗？米歇尔的观点遭受了猛烈的抨击，批评者认为他的研究方法低估了人格在不同情况下的一致性（Epstein，1980）。贝姆和艾伦（Bem & Allen，1974）还指出，有些人的行为比其他人的更稳定。此外，当有其他人在场（Kenrick & Stringfeld，1980）或在熟悉的情况下时，行为的一致性最强（Funder，1983a，1983b；Funder & Ozer，1983）。
p67.en: Michelle's claims challenge the very foundation of the majority doctrine. After all, what is the merit of the personality theory if people are acting differently in different situations? Is there no continuity in personality? Michelle's point of view has been strongly criticized, and critics have argued that his research methods underestimate the consistency of personality in different contexts (Epstein, 1980). Bhem and Allen (Bem & Allen, 1974) also noted that some people acted more steadily than others. In addition, when other persons are present (Kenrick & Stringfeld, 1980) or in familiar circumstances, the conduct is most consistent (Funder, 1983a, 1983b); Funder & Ozer, 1983.

p68.original: 虽然人格-情境争论动摇了人格心理学的基础，但促进了社会心理学的发展。在社会心理学中，心理学家一直在论证情境的力量。在一些特殊的情境领域，正常的大学生可以变成骗子、情人，甚至是残忍的施虐者。那么，在面对人格-情境争论时，我们能得到哪些启示呢？
p68.en: Although the personality-situation debate has shaken the foundations of personality psychology, it has contributed to the development of socio-psychology. In the sociopsychology, psychologists have been demonstrating the power of the situation. In some specific situations, regular university students can become liars, lovers and even cruel abusers. So, what can we get when we face a personality-situation dispute?

p70.original: 这不是一个非此即彼的问题，我们不是要争论行为是由特质决定的还是由环境决定的。准确地说，这是一个谁的影响更大及什么时候影响更大的问题。针对人格-情境进行争论的各方都认为人格和情境都会起作用。在这个问题上，争论的焦点其实是想确定哪一方面的影响更大。
p70.en: It is not a question of whether or not to do so, and we are not arguing whether the conduct is determined by the quality of the act or the environment. To be precise, it is a question of who has more influence and when. The parties to the debate about the personality-situation are of the view that both the personality and the situation work. The debate on this issue is really focused on determining which aspects have a greater impact.

p71.original: 这里还有第二个问题：在不同的情境下，人格特质的作用有多大？在极端情况下，如单独监禁的囚犯，情境显然更重要。但对日常生活中的普通人来说，与人格特质相比，情境的影响有多大？这并不是一个容易回答的问题。
p71.en: Here is the second question: What is the role of personality in different situations? In extreme cases, such as prisoners held incommunicado, the situation is clearly more important. But for ordinary people in everyday life, what is the impact of the situation as compared to the character of the person? This is not an easy question to answer.

p73.original: 如果长期观察一个人，我们可能会发现，他会在不同的场合对相同的情境做出不一样的反应。回想一下：当去你最喜欢的餐厅时，你总是点同样的东西吗？你和你的朋友总是相处得很愉快吗？特质心理学家提醒我们，人格特质是一个人的习惯行为的平均表现（一般来说，也许你和朋友相处时总是快乐的）。
p73.en: If we look at a person for a long time, we may find that he will respond differently to the same situation on different occasions. Think back: When you go to your favorite restaurant, do you always order the same thing? Do you and your friends always have a good time? Characteristic psychologists remind us that the character of the person is the average expression of a person's customary behaviour (generally, perhaps you're always happy with your friends).

p74.original: 当人们从一种情境转换到另一种情境时，他们的行为是一致的还是相差很大呢？在一项研究中，参与者会每天多次记录他们所处的情境和行为，并在大五人格量表上进行自我评估。研究发现：当人们从一种情境转换到另一种情境时，他们描述的自我人格特质会像他们的行为一样发生根本性变化（Fleeson，2004）。
p74.en: Is it true that when people change from one situation to another, their behaviour is uniform or very different? In one study, participants recorded their situations and behaviours on several occasions a day and self-assessments were carried out on the five-person scale. The study found that when people change from one situation to another, they describe a fundamental change in their self-personal characteristics as their behaviour (Fleeson, 2004).

p75.original: 在这里我们学到的是，虽然影响行为的因素有很多种，但其中很多因素不能简单地划分为人格因素或情境因素。行为是特质和情境相互作用的结果（Kenrick & Funder，1988）。事实上，米歇尔从未主张我们应当抛下人格理论。相反，他认为行为是由情境、个人对情境的认识以及人格共同决定的（Mischel，1990，2003；Mischel & Shoda，1995）。
p75.en: What we have learned here is that while there are many factors that influence behaviour, many of them cannot simply be classified as personal or contextual. The behaviour is the result of the interaction between the quality and the context (Kenrick & Funder, 1988). In fact, Michelle never argued that we should leave the theory of personality behind. On the contrary, he considers that the conduct is determined by circumstances, individual perceptions of the situation, and common personality (Mischel, 1990, 2003); Mischel & Shoda, 1995.

p76.original: 人的变化也取决于情境的具体类型
p76.en: The changes in humans depend on the specific type of situation.

p77.original: 熟悉情境和陌生情境对人的影响是不一样的。如果是熟悉的情境，那么一个人会展现出其惯常的行为模式，我们也能够通过对其人格的了解来合理准确地预测他的行为。然而，在陌生的情境中，原有的行为习惯可能是不合适的。人们会通过观察别人来找到合适的行为方式，此时，情境的影响大于人格差异。
p77.en: The human impact of familiarity and unfamiliarity is different. If a familiar situation exists, then a person can display his or her usual pattern of behaviour and we can predict his or her behaviour reasonably and accurately by knowing his or her personality. However, in strange situations, pre-existing behavioural habits may not be appropriate. People find the right way to behave by looking at others, and the impact of the situation is greater than the difference in personality.

p78.original: 我们能够得出什么结论？

p79.original: 在人格-情境争论中，哪一方是正确的呢？其实，双方各有其正确的方面。根据人格心理学家威廉·弗利森（William Fleeson）在2004年的研究结果，当人格具有一致性时，人格特质有助于我们理解长期的行为。但是，在较短的时期内，特别是在特定的情境下，一个人的行为可能非常不稳定。所以，从长远来看，特质观更合适；而在某一时刻，情境观更合适。
p79.en: Which side is right in the personality-situation dispute? In fact, each side has its own aspects. According to the findings of William Fleeson, a personality psychologist in 2004, when personality is consistent, personality qualities help us to understand behaviour over time. However, in a relatively short period of time, especially in specific situations, the behaviour of an individual may be very volatile. So, in the long run, the quality perspective is more appropriate; And at one point, the situation is more appropriate.

p80.original: 但是，如米歇尔所说，哪一方的影响更大还取决于情境的强弱。更复杂的是，我们也需要将文化作为情境的一部分考虑进去。有证据表明，在个体主义文化中，个体的人格特质对行为的影响比在集体主义文化中更大（Church et al.，2006）。因此，我们会看到，在个体主义文化中会更看重某些特质，如智力（而非努力工作）。当然，在集体主义文化中，由于更强调情境的作用，人们更不容易犯基本归因错误。
p80.en: However, as Michelle said, which side has a greater impact depends on the strength and weakness of the situation. More complicated is the need to take culture into account as part of the context. There is evidence that in an individualistic culture, the personality of the individual has a greater influence on behaviour than in a collective culture (Church et al., 2006). Thus, we can see that in the culture of individualism certain qualities, such as intelligence (rather than hard work), are given greater weight. Of course, in a collectiveist culture, greater emphasis on the role of the situation makes it more difficult for people to make basic attribution mistakes.

p81.original: 结束语：你自己及周围环境的独特性
p81.en: Concluding remarks: The uniqueness of yourself and the surrounding environment

p82.original: 我们以一个问题来结束本章。
p82.en: We conclude this chapter with a question.

p83.original: 你知道在整个已知的宇宙中有哪三件事物是独一无二的吗？
p83.en: Do you know what three things are unique in the entire known universe?

p84.original: 这意味着它们具有可观察和可测量的特征，用以反映它们的独特性，而这些独特性是其他同类事物所没有的。
p84.en: This means that they have observable and measurable features that reflect their uniqueness, which is not present in other things of the same kind.

p85.original: 在人类世界里，它们是指纹。在物理宇宙中，它们是雪花。在心理学世界里，它们是人格。让我们进行进一步的讨论。
p85.en: In the human world, they are fingerprints. In the physical universe, they're snowflakes. In the world of psychology, they are human beings. Let us have a further discussion.

p86.original: 雪花的独特性是科学家们拍摄了数百万片新飘落的雪花后发现的。虽然雪花有各种大小和形状，但是他们没有观察到有相同图案的雪花。当雪花出现在不同的温度和湿度的条件下时，会形成复杂的形状，因此每一片雪花的结构几乎都是独一无二的。在1988年，学者南希·奈特（Nancy Knight）在美国国家大气研究中心（National Center for Atmospheric Research）研究雪花时，发现了两片完全相同的空心柱状雪花，这对“没有两片雪花是完全相同的”这一说法提出了挑战。但需要注意的是，这只是几百万片雪花中的两个，所以我们仍然认为每一片雪花都是非常独特的！
p86.en: The uniqueness of snowflakes is discovered by scientists who film millions of new snowflakes. Although snowflakes have various sizes and shapes, they do not observe snowflakes with the same pattern. When snowflakes occur at different temperature and humidity conditions, they form complex shapes, so that the structure of each snowflake is almost unique. In 1988, Nancy Knight, a scholar, found two identical hollow column-shaped snowflakes when studying snowflakes at the National Center for American Research, challenging the assertion that “no two snowflakes are identical”. But what needs to be noted is that it's only two of the millions of snowflakes, so we still think that each snowflake is unique!

p87.original: “指纹的独特性”这一说法由来已久。1888年，才华横溢的弗朗西斯·高尔顿（Francis Galton）曾这样描述指纹：
p87.en: The term “uniqueness of fingerprints” has a long history. In 1888, Francis Galton, a talented man, described the fingerprints as follows:

p88.original: 在约0.066立方米的人体肌肉、脂肪以及骨骼中，有许多需要或不需要借助显微镜被观察到的指纹。也许所有浅层中最美丽和最具特色的是那些中间有脊的小沟纹和毛孔，它们在手和脚的表皮下的排列异常复杂又均匀有序（Nature，June28，1888）。
p88.en: In approximately 0.066 cubic metres of human muscles, fats and bones, there are many fingerprints that need or need not be observed with microscopes. Perhaps the most beautiful and distinctive of all shallow layers are those with ridges and fur holes, which are extremely complex and evenly organized under the skin of their hands and feet (Nature, June 28, 1888).

p89.original: 美国联邦调查局和其他执法机构一致认为：在收集和检查了数百万枚指纹之后，没有任何两枚指纹的模式是相同的，即使是同卵双胞胎的指纹。
p89.en: The Federal Bureau of Investigation and other law enforcement agencies in the United States agreed that, after millions of fingerprints had been collected and examined, no two fingerprints were modelled in the same way, even for identical twins.

p90.original: 正如我们在本章中看到的，人格心理学研究试图揭示每个人的内在特征。是什么将个体与大多数人甚至所有人区别开来？人格心理学家在内在体验上（而不是外貌上）寻找这些差异。内在体验包括内在倾向、特质以及性格特征，这些结合起来形成了独一无二的每个人。
p90.en: As we have seen in this chapter, the study of personality psychology attempts to reveal the intrinsic characteristics of each individual. What distinguishes an individual from most and even all? Personal psychologists look for these differences in their experience (not in their physical appearance). Inherent experiences include internal tendencies, characteristics and character characteristics that combine to create a unique individual.

p91.original: 你可能会想，这种方法与我们研究心理学的其他方法非常不同，因为其他方法试图揭示人们在相同环境下的一般行为模式。在某种程度上，你是对的。为了了解人格，研究人员采取了一些方法来评估世界各地人们的共同特征或相似的行为模式，这就产生了一个悖论，毕竟我们每个人都相信自己具有独特性。对于主要关注个人、全人及自我的心理学家而言，探索人的共性和独特性是他们永恒的主题。
p91.en: You might think that this approach is very different from the other methods of our study of psychology, which try to reveal the general patterns of behaviour of people in the same environment. In a way, you're right. In order to understand the personality, researchers have adopted a number of methods to assess the common characteristics or similar patterns of behaviour of people around the world, which has led to the paradox that each of us believes in its own uniqueness. For psychologists who focus primarily on individuals, the whole person and themselves, exploring the commonality and uniqueness of human beings is their permanent theme.
